findings.description: The Colab warning also fires when refresh_rate == 0. A value of 0 turns the progress bar off, so warning that it may crash is misleading. The condition should be `IS_COLAB and 0 < refresh_rate < 20`.

The warning is checked before looking at whether the user passed their own ProgressBarBase callback. In that case the Trainer's refresh_rate is never used. Example: Trainer(callbacks=[ProgressBar(refresh_rate=50)]) keeps the default refresh_rate=1 and still gets a misleading warning. The check should only apply when a default ProgressBar is created from refresh_rate.

The feature request asks to change the refresh rate to 20 automatically on Colab when the user keeps the default. This PR only adds a warning. Because the default is 1, every Colab user running a plain pl.Trainer() now gets a warning and keeps the crash-prone setting, which is the confusing case for beginners the request wanted to avoid. Consider making the default None and resolving it to 20 on Colab and 1 elsewhere.

IS_COLAB is a constant computed at import time. If google.colab is imported after pytorch_lightning, the check misses it. It is also hard to monkeypatch in tests because callback_connector imports the value directly. No test was added for the new warning.
